content: Browser WebTorrent swarms are bandwidth-symmetric to the browser tab (no NAT traversal issues since WebRTC handles it, but limited to WebRTC-capable peers/web-seeds); server-side torrent engines (librqbit) bear full swarm bandwidth on the host machine but reach the whole normal BitTorrent swarm (TCP/UDP peers, DHT) and can reuse existing HTTP relay/CORS infrastructure. Hybrid approach (server-side engine, HTTP range streaming to browser) avoids WebRTC/NAT/CORS complexity entirely by treating torrent-as-a-source the same as any HTTP VOD source.
